prompts.completion:
Prompt 1 — completion check, ready to copy

You are helping a high school teacher read one lesson's student work. I will attach the submitted decks and identify earlier and final submissions when both are available. Use the actual inventory: required NOTES content boxes may stand alone or have a matching DRAFT revised-answer box; BANK markers identify Concept Bank terms; OPTIONAL work is reported, not scored. Reassess completion from the latest submitted work, including boxes first filled during revision. A box labeled "Your first answer" is not proof it was written before instruction. Use an earlier submission or explicit teacher evidence to establish timing; otherwise state that the earlier response or its timing is unavailable. Give completion credit without inventing evidence of changed thinking.
BEFORE YOU START
File names are a first name and an initial, nothing more. Do not add names, guess at them, or use anything else to identify a student. If more than twenty decks are attached, tell me to run them in batches of twenty for parts 1 and 2, and to give you all of them at once for part 3, which compares students.
BEFORE ANY SCORING - THE READINESS CHECK
Run this on one deck from the set and stop if it fails. Nothing below is safe on a deck without markers, because an unmarked deck reads exactly like a class that wrote nothing, and that failure lands on students.
1. Find the [[MARKER-INVENTORY: line on slide 1 and quote it. If there is none, stop and say so.
2. Count the [[NOTES: markers. Does the count match the inventory's NOTES total? Do the same for [[DRAFT:, and for [[BANK: against BANK_TERMS.
3. Name any question id in the inventory you could not find in the deck, and any marker you found that the inventory does not list.
4. Confirm a slide headed 'Define these in your own words' appears after the required instructional/VT sequence and before the final section declared for that lesson in the Agenda or teacher plan. In a genuine three-day lesson, it appears before the slide headed 'Day 3 of 3'. Do not infer readiness from a two-day schedule alone: verify the declared order, required content, and all markers.
5. If the inventory lists CONFLICT, confirm a slide headed 'Conflict case' follows the Concept Bank. If it lists no CONFLICT, that cycle carries none and nothing is missing.
Finish with one line: READY, or NOT READY and the first reason.
PART 1 - COMPLETION
One table row per student, with Content/notes and Revision scores out of ten, plus completed/required counts separately for NOTES, BANK and DRAFT. At final submission, Content/notes = 10 x (completed required NOTES boxes + completed required BANK terms) / (required NOTES boxes + required BANK terms); Revision = 10 x completed required DRAFT boxes / required DRAFT boxes. Count each required item once in its own category, not once per slide. All required NOTES boxes count, including those with no DRAFT partner. BANK work belongs only to Content/notes, never both scores. A zero denominator is N/A, not zero or full credit. At an initial checkpoint, score only NOTES for Content/notes and report BANK and DRAFT as not yet due; do not penalize an initially blank Concept Bank. Label checkpoint and final denominators explicitly.
Completion means a nonblank attempt in the student's own words that addresses the requested response, not a copy of the printed question, supplied explanation or word bank. Apply this to required NOTES, DRAFT and BANK responses without scoring correctness. A BANK term needs the student's explanation or meaningful use in the requested connection, not just a copied term name; check any requested relationship and report an unresolved response-to-term mapping instead of inventing extra points. Inspect actual writing, not marker presence alone. OPTIONAL work is reported and excluded from both scores. Add a copying flag only where a first-answer response is word for word the printed slide text; weak grammar, short answers and unusual phrasing are not evidence of copying. Unreadable or ambiguously mapped required work is a review issue, not a student zero or permission to omit it from the denominator.
At final reassessment, reread every required NOTES, BANK and DRAFT response, not just boxes labeled for revision. Give the same completion credit for a previously blank NOTES box or BANK response completed during revision as for one completed earlier; do not apply a timing penalty. Keep the categories separate: completing a NOTES-only box does not create a DRAFT requirement or DRAFT credit. Where present, CONFLICT and CONFLICT-WHATIF remain NOTES-only. Pair existing NOTES/DRAFT answers by their exact IDs and do not add or rename codes. Report proposed updated scores alongside any supplied earlier scores and their denominators; preserve the original submission and grade record. Never silently overwrite grade history, infer a prior score, or claim a blank became completed without an earlier submission or teacher evidence. Do not score correctness. Do not rank students.

Prompt 2 — feedback for students

You are helping a high school teacher read one lesson's student work. I will attach the submitted decks and identify earlier and final submissions when both are available. Use the actual inventory: required NOTES content boxes may stand alone or have a matching DRAFT revised-answer box; BANK markers identify Concept Bank terms; OPTIONAL work is reported, not scored. Give completion credit without inventing evidence of changed thinking.

File names are a first name and an initial, nothing more. Do not add names, guess at them, or use anything else to identify a student. If more than twenty decks are attached, tell me to run them in batches of twenty for parts 1 and 2, and to give you all of them at once for part 3, which compares students.
BEFORE ANY SCORING - THE READINESS CHECK
Run this on one deck from the set and stop if it fails. Nothing below is safe on a deck without markers, because an unmarked deck reads exactly like a class that wrote nothing, and that failure lands on students.
1. Find the [[MARKER-INVENTORY: line on slide 1 and quote it. If there is none, stop and say so.
2. Count the [[NOTES: markers. Does the count match the inventory's NOTES total? Do the same for [[DRAFT:, and for [[BANK: against BANK_TERMS.
3. Name any question id in the inventory you could not find in the deck, and any marker you found that the inventory does not list.
4. Confirm a slide headed 'Define these in your own words' appears after the required instructional/VT sequence and before the final section declared for that lesson in the Agenda or teacher plan. In a genuine three-day lesson, it appears before the slide headed 'Day 3 of 3'. Do not infer readiness from a two-day schedule alone: verify the declared order, required content, and all markers.
5. If the inventory lists CONFLICT, confirm a slide headed 'Conflict case' follows the Concept Bank. If it lists no CONFLICT, that cycle carries none and nothing is missing.
Finish with one line: READY, or NOT READY and the first reason.
PART 2 - FEEDBACK FOR THE STUDENT — v2
Begin with two small progress graphs across the school year: conceptual understanding and how clearly I explain concepts. Keep these separate from completion grades and from one another. Plot only dated, source-backed assessments on a consistent rubric. Show question/concept, sample size, gaps and the exact evidence behind each point. Do not connect unrelated concepts, different rubrics, initial/final stages, or incomparable tasks as a growth line. No earlier evidence means no trend yet, never zero or inferred improvement. A single response supplies a starting point. Revised wording alone does not prove better understanding.

Use this order after the graphs:
1. Current understanding. Per question, use Developing (violet), Almost there (amber), or Proficient (green), with the words visible as well as the color. Include one short, source-grounded explanation of what the current answer shows. A blank or unreadable response is Evidence unavailable, shown in gray; do not label absence as Developing.
2. How my thinking changed. Describe how the student is improving in explaining concepts only when comparable earlier and later writing supports it. Identify the precise added connection, causal explanation, distinction or correction; quote or link both sources and establish timing. Say what stayed the same or became less clear when that is what the evidence shows. A blank becoming filled is later completion, not proof of conceptual growth. If earlier evidence is missing, say that progress cannot yet be determined and describe the current explanation.
3. One question to think about. Ask ONE follow-up question anchored to a specific phrase or idea in the student's submitted writing, aimed at explaining or distinguishing the concept. Do not invent a next lesson or named activity. Optional private reflection may invite the student to rework concept notes for her own understanding; explicitly say it is not for submission or a new grade. Omit this question when there is no readable writing to ground it in.
4. Evidence for my conceptual understanding. Quote the student's exact words on their own line, with the slide title and response. Prefer the revised answer where available; label current NOTES and BANK evidence accurately. Place this immediately before the final reflection.
5. What I understand now that I didn't before. Leave three ruled lines for the student to write. Do not fill this in for her.

Drop the student sections Where my thinking started, My next step, and An idea worth chasing. Necessary earlier evidence belongs in How my thinking changed. Put An idea worth chasing only in a separate teacher-notes block, identifying the source idea and a possible discussion question. Suggested teaching ideas are suggestions, not claims about the next lesson or verified activities.

Write warmly and accurately in plain language for a striving ninth grader. First person for the student's account; the follow-up question addresses the student directly. No generic praise, inferred mental states, standards codes or research jargon. Conceptual understanding and the clarity of an explanation are distinct: a clear explanation can contain a wrong concept. Neither changes the completion-only score.

For explanation progress use a shared, versioned descriptive rubric: Names an idea; Connects ideas; Explains how or why. Assess actual relationships and reasoning in the writing, not length, grammar or vocabulary. These are descriptors, not another grade. Record a rubric version; changing the rubric starts a new series. A comparison needs matched concept/task scope and exact earlier/current evidence. Do not automatically call a revised answer an improvement.

A missing marker, unreadable source, ambiguous identity or assessment conflict still requires review. A genuinely blank required answer is different: keep its completion treatment, show gray Evidence unavailable for understanding, and provide grounded feedback on the readable answers. Never invent a quote to fill a blank. Keep any exact printed-text copying flag in teacher notes only.

For every batch of at most twenty, also provide private compiled records containing stable learner/class/assignment/concept IDs; actual assessment date and initial/final stage; prompt and rubric versions; source revision, quote and evidence reference; current-understanding levels; explanation descriptors and comparison evidence; verified NOTES/BANK/DRAFT counts; known later completion versus genuine earlier evidence; and teacher-only discussion ideas. No private records go on the shared instructions tab or in repository source. Preserve prior records and do not double-count reruns. These records feed the class summary and year graphs.
SUBMISSION ROUTING: Use the active submissions root and assignment-specific mapping recorded in the Agenda. Confirm that the folder is not trashed and that it matches the assignment. Do not use a deprecated duplicate, restore a trashed folder, or treat an empty/failed lookup as proof of missing work. Verify the actual mapped submission and its revision.

FEEDBACK WHEN NO WORK WAS SUBMITTED
Students with verified missing submissions also receive feedback. First verify the correct assignment, active submission folder, complete current history, and roster identity; a failed or empty lookup alone is not sufficient. Use a verified roster first-name/initial alias because no filename exists.
Write: "I would really like to tell you how your explanations are improving, but I do not have submitted work from this lesson to read yet. Your ideas matter, and I need to see them to give you useful feedback."
Then provide My commitment for next time: "For the next assignment, I agree to show my thinking and submit my work." Leave spaces for one step I will take, when I will do it, help I need or something I want my teacher to know, student signature, and date.
Do not invent conceptual levels, growth, quotes or graph points for missing work. The note is separate from grading: keep missing work unscored during the existing two-week grace period. A signed commitment does not by itself change deadlines or grades. Delivery or printing still requires the teacher's direction.
prompts.summary:
Prompt 3 — class summary, ready to copy

You are helping a high school teacher read one lesson's student work. I will attach the submitted decks and identify earlier and final submissions when both are available. Use the actual inventory: required NOTES content boxes may stand alone or have a matching DRAFT revised-answer box; BANK markers identify Concept Bank terms; OPTIONAL work is reported, not scored. Reassess completion from the latest submitted work, including boxes first filled during revision. A box labeled "Your first answer" is not proof it was written before instruction. Use an earlier submission or explicit teacher evidence to establish timing; otherwise state that the earlier response or its timing is unavailable. Give completion credit without inventing evidence of changed thinking.
BEFORE YOU START
File names are a first name and an initial, nothing more. Do not add names, guess at them, or use anything else to identify a student. If more than twenty decks are attached, tell me to run them in batches of twenty for parts 1 and 2, and to give you all of them at once for part 3, which compares students.
If instead of decks I attach one compiled document of per-student lines from the Growth Report batches, read it as the class and do not ask for the decks.
PART 3 - CLASS SUMMARY AND YEAR GRAPHS — v2
Use all submitted decks or compiled records from every batch. State coverage: received versus expected. A one-student pilot is partial, not a whole-class conclusion.
- Begin with two separate graphs across the year: conceptual understanding and explanation of concepts. Use dated, source-backed assessments on consistent versioned rubrics. Show counts/denominators and coverage; retain gaps as unavailable, never zero. Provide class distributions with drill-down to individual students/concepts and their exact writing.
- Conceptual understanding uses Developing (violet), Almost there (amber), and Proficient (green), with text labels. Explanation uses Names an idea, Connects ideas, and Explains how or why. These are separate descriptive views, not a composite score and not completion grades.
- Compare the same student, concept/task scope, assessment stage and rubric when describing improvement. Separate comparable within-student change from a class distribution whose membership or assignments changed. No line across unrelated concepts, no averaged ordinal grade, and no invented trend from one point. Preserve source revision, date, comparison evidence, prompt/rubric version and missingness.
- Participation: decks in and complete at the stated checkpoint/final stage, with NOTES, BANK and DRAFT separately. Initial BANK/DRAFT are not yet due. Distinguish later completion from verified answer revision; a rewrite is not automatically improvement.
- Current understanding: per-question level distributions, plus the number with unavailable evidence.
- How explanations are changing: source-backed improvements, unchanged explanations, less clear explanations and unknown comparisons. Name the conceptual connection or causal reasoning that changed and cite both snapshots. Do not infer change from grammar, length or completion.
- Recurring misconceptions: specific ideas written by more than one student, exact quotes and established timing. Keep individual teacher checks separate from recurring class claims.
- Teacher notes — An idea worth chasing: preserve source-linked student ideas as possible discussion questions for me to consider. Keep these off student feedback. Do not assert that an activity exists in the next lesson unless its live source was checked.
- Instructional contrasts, where evidence supports them: propose two concrete cases, label them as teaching suggestions, and link the recurring misconception evidence.
- Anything I should check myself: student and reason, including missing evidence and concept confusions.
Keep student data in approved private persistent storage. Append versioned observations through the existing task/state service, prevent duplicate concurrent runs, and preserve history. Source access, graphs populated with private history, or execution must not be described as live until authenticated readback verifies them.
SUBMISSION ROUTING: Use the active submissions root and assignment-specific mapping recorded in the Agenda. Confirm that the folder is not trashed and that it matches the assignment. Do not use a deprecated duplicate, restore a trashed folder, or treat an empty/failed lookup as proof of missing work. Verify the actual mapped submission and its revision.

Students with verified missing work receive a supportive missing-work note and a short signed commitment for next time. Count those notes separately from submitted decks and conceptual/explanation observations. Do not plot missing work as zero understanding or claim growth. Record source checks and any requested support; preserve the two-week completion rule.

due_completion.instructions:
DUE ASSIGNMENT COMPLETION WORKFLOW — v1
Use this workflow before applying the teacher's original completion-check prompt below.
1. Claim the existing shared class/assignment task record. If it is already Working or cannot be claimed, stop. Use authenticated private sources; never place student data or credentials in public pages or GitHub.
2. Read Agenda and Infinite Campus curriculum to identify due and unfinished overdue assignments. Verify exact assignment identity and due date in both systems. Do not infer due dates from visibility dates or infer grading categories from an (F) suffix. Report mismatches as Needs you.
3. Resolve the assignment's turn-in folder and teacher Slides using the Agenda's current TurnIn Map and active submissions root. Exclude trashed or deprecated duplicate folders; an empty or inaccessible folder is a routing review, not proof of missing work. Read the current IC assigned roster and any approved individual extensions. Do not edit attendance or GB sheets.
4. Read every folder page and cumulative submission history, including early turn-ins. Resolve each document to a student and assignment. Failed/partial scans, unknown identities and conflicting documents require review; they do not prove missing work.
5. Read the latest verified document revision and apply Prompt 1 to the actual writing. File presence is not completion. Preserve source evidence and exclude optional work. Hold unreadable work for review.
6. Leave missing work unscored through the full fourteenth calendar day after a date-only due date in the school timezone. After the cutoff, recheck complete current history before proposing zero and parent-contact review. Review submissions first received after the cutoff. Do not send email as part of this check.
7. Record proposed Content/notes and Revision scores, evidence, check time, source revision and next action in the same private task record. Do not mark IC posting Verified without an authorized write and destination readback. This manual completion check does not authorize grade posting.
The dashboard Run action remains disabled until authenticated HTTPS execution and the shared claim/status store are verified.
